_note: OSCE station D3 — converted from embla-cases ddx-p-anaphylaxis-1 v1.0.0 (sha256:dae926c523d9caa9). Presentation follows the deploy-safe form for the reaction itself (seafood exposure, urticaria, facial swelling, cramping gut, expiratory wheeze); per the season design (Station Sets v2 declared this member paediatric) the patient is re-aged to a six-year-old of twenty kilograms — the source case's adult frame does not carry the set's teaching point, and the note says so rather than hiding it. The hidden block informed only the rubric (demo/rubrics/osce-d3.json). Clinically shaped, not clinically reviewed. The season's first disease returns one last time, child-sized: the drug is the same, the dose is not. Weigh her, then draw 0.01 mg per kilo — the adult half-milligram is the classic pitfall, and here it is a scored harm even though she survives it. The adrenaline family sits first in the list so a dosed order is read as a dose, never as small talk about kilograms.

effects.beat: adrenaline 0.2 mg im, outer thigh — 0.01 a kilo, drawn to the twenty she weighs

interventions.label: Adrenaline 0.5 mg IM — adult dose (HARM)
interventions.harm: half a milligram into a twenty-kilo child — an adult dose, two and a half times hers; the tachycardia that follows is yours

interventions.label: IV-push adrenaline (HARM)
interventions.harm: iv push adrenaline — arrhythmia on a small beating heart

effects.beat: the nurse holds the ampoule still: "how much, doctor? she is twenty kilos." the drug waits on a number.
— "Twenty kilos, on the school scales last week," her mother says, already half-crying. The number every dose hangs on.
— "Prawn fritters at the school fair. She knows she mustn't — she is six, she forgot to ask." Thirty minutes ago.
— "Shrimp, since she was two. It is written on a card in her school bag."
wheals climbing her neck and arms, lips swelling as you watch — she keeps licking them
expiratory wheeze both sides, tugging under the little ribs
saline 20 mils a kilo — four hundred, warmed, running through a small pink cannula
antihistamine for the itch — after the adrenaline, never instead of it
steroid on board — for the late phase
anaphylaxis — the season's first disease, child-sized

interventions.label: Admit and watch for the second wave

effects.beat: admitted with mum on the bed beside her — the biphasic wave finds the nurses ready

interventions.label: Send her home (HARM)
interventions.harm: discharged during the observation window — biphasic reactions come back to children asleep in cars

do.harm: adrenaline delayed — a child's airway closes faster than the argument about the dose

outcomes.label: Weighed, dosed to the kilo, watched — home with a junior auto-injector
The smallest airway in the building, and the drug never came
